protocol_claim_en: Lower blood glucose/insulin to 'starve' cancer (metabolic therapy framing).
risk_flags: Overgeneralization risk; depends on cancer type/treatment status; avoid 'cure' claims.

key_evidence.citation: Warburg O. On the origin of cancer cells. Science. 1956.
Pollak M. Insulin and insulin-like growth factor signalling in neoplasia. Nat Rev Cancer. 2008.

protocol_claim_en: Use low-dose aspirin around cancer care (anti-inflammatory/anti-metastatic).
risk_flags: Bleeding risk; drug interactions (anticoagulants, chemo); perioperative timing matters.

key_evidence.citation: Rothwell PM et al. Effect of daily aspirin on risk of cancer metastasis. Lancet. 2012.

protocol_claim_en: Metformin as anti-cancer adjunct (repurposed diabetes drug).
risk_flags: Lactic acidosis risk in certain conditions; renal/hepatic issues; drug interactions.

key_evidence.citation: Evans JMM et al. Metformin and reduced risk of cancer in diabetic patients. BMJ. 2005.

protocol_claim_en: Berberine for metabolic control (and indirectly cancer-related).
risk_flags: Supplement-drug interactions; pregnancy/arrhythmia/liver concerns; product variability.

key_evidence.citation: Yin J et al. Efficacy of berberine in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. Metabolism. 2008.

protocol_claim_en: Cimetidine as immune-modulating adjunct in colorectal cancer.
risk_flags: Off-label use; interactions (e.g., CYP effects); should be clinician-led.

key_evidence.citation: Matsumoto S. Cimetidine and survival with colorectal cancer. Lancet. 1995.
Kelly MD et al. Randomized trial of preoperative cimetidine in patients with colorectal cancer. Br J Surg. 1999.

protocol_claim_en: IV high-dose vitamin C selectively harms cancer cells.
risk_flags: Medical infusion risks; kidney stones/renal issues; G6PD deficiency hemolysis risk.

key_evidence.citation: Chen Q et al. Pharmacologic ascorbic acid concentrations selectively kill cancer cells. PNAS. 2005.

protocol_claim_en: Fasting / fasting-mimicking diet (FMD) around chemo improves outcomes or tolerance.
risk_flags: Malnutrition risk; eating-disorder risk; treatment-specific safety concerns.

key_evidence.citation: de Groot S et al. Fasting mimicking diet as an adjunct to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer. 2020.

protocol_claim_en: Ketogenic diet as 'no-glucose' strategy to weaken tumors.
risk_flags: Weight loss/malnutrition; lipid issues; not appropriate for many patients.

key_evidence.citation: Römer M et al. The use of ketogenic diets in cancer patients: a systematic review. 2021.
Amaral LJ et al. Phase 1 trial of ketogenic diet plus standard of care in glioblastoma. 2025.

protocol_claim_en: Ferroptosis as a therapeutic angle (iron-dependent cell death).
risk_flags: High risk of speculative protocolization; avoid prescriptive dosing recommendations.

key_evidence.citation: Dixon SJ et al. Ferroptosis: an iron-dependent form of nonapoptotic cell death. Cell. 2012.

protocol_claim_en: Repurposed cardiovascular drugs (statins/dipyridamole) have anti-cancer effects.
risk_flags: Off-label; drug interactions; bleeding risk (dipyridamole).

key_evidence.citation: Jeong GH et al. Statin and cancer mortality/survival: an umbrella review. 2020.
Huang S et al. Dipyridamole enhances the anti-cancer ability of aspirin against colorectal cancer (preclinical). 2023.

protocol_claim_en: DCA (dichloroacetate) as metabolic anti-cancer therapy.
risk_flags: Neurotoxicity; off-label; sourcing/purity issues if obtained outside trils.

key_evidence.citation: Dunbar EM et al. Phase 1 trial of DCA in malignant gliomas/brain metastases. 2014.
Tataranni T et al. DCA and cancer: overview. 2019.

protocol_claim_en: For people with certain MTHFR variants and/or low B12 status, using folic acid instead of 5-MTHF (L-methylfolate) may worsen unmetabolized folic acid exposure and can complicate methylation/homocysteine management; supplementation choices should be guided by labs and clinical context rather than genotype alone.
risk_flags: Overgeneralization risk; many MTHFR variants have small effects; cancer outcomes not established; avoid anti-fortification narratives; requires clinician oversight.

key_evidence.citation: Weathers SP et al. Nat Commun. 2025 (used here only as corpus context; not primary evidence for folate/MTHFR claims).

protocol_claim_en: In a single-arm phase I/II trial of newly diagnosed glioblastoma, adding the anti–PD-L1 antibody atezolizumab to standard radiation and temozolomide was feasible and associated with a median overall survival of approximately 18 months.
risk_flags: Single-arm trial; no randomized control; survival comparisons are historical; association does not prove treatment benefit.

key_evidence.citation: Weathers SP et al. Improved overall survival in an anti-PD-L1 treated cohort of newly diagnosed glioblastoma patients. Nat Commun. 2025.

protocol_claim_en: MGMT promoter methylation status stratified survival in the anti–PD-L1-treated glioblastoma cohort, with longer overall survival observed in MGMT-methylated tumors.
risk_flags: MGMT is a known prognostic and predictive marker for temozolomide response; effect is not specific proof of PD-L1 benefit.

key_evidence.citation: Weathers SP et al. Nat Commun. 2025.

protocol_claim_en: Exploratory genomic clustering in anti–PD-L1-treated glioblastoma identified a PTEN-mutant tumor cluster associated with longer overall survival compared with an EGFR-enriched cluster.
risk_flags: Exploratory analysis; small subset; clustering-derived association; not causal; requires independent validation.

key_evidence.citation: Weathers SP et al. Nat Commun. 2025.

protocol_claim_en: Longer survival following anti–PD-L1 therapy in glioblastoma was associated with enrichment of immune-related transcriptomic programs, including interferon-gamma signaling, antigen presentation, and inflammatory response signatures.
risk_flags: Transcriptomic associations do not establish mechanism; immune activation does not guarantee therapeutic response.

key_evidence.citation: Weathers SP et al. Nat Commun. 2025.

protocol_claim_en: Baseline tumor immune score was associated with overall survival in the anti–PD-L1-treated glioblastoma cohort but not in external non-immunotherapy glioblastoma cohorts, suggesting treatment-context specificity.
risk_flags: Cross-cohort comparisons are confounded by platform and treatment differences; context-specificity is a hypothesis.

key_evidence.citation: Weathers SP et al. Nat Commun. 2025.

protocol_claim_en: In anti–PD-L1-treated glioblastoma patients, baseline gut microbiome composition differed between longer- and shorter-survival groups, suggesting a potential association between microbiome features and immunotherapy response.
risk_flags: Exploratory association only; small subset with fecal samples; specific taxa not validated; highly confounded by diet, antibiotics, corticosteroids, and geography.

key_evidence.citation: Weathers SP et al. Improved overall survival in an anti-PD-L1 treated cohort of newly diagnosed glioblastoma patients. Nat Commun. 2025.

protocol_claim_en: Immune checkpoint inhibitors generally show limited efficacy in glioblastoma due to low tumor mutational burden, an immunosuppressive myeloid-dominated tumor microenvironment, limited T-cell infiltration, and the effects of corticosteroids.
risk_flags: Applies to population-level outcomes; does not preclude benefit in molecularly or immunologically selected subgroups.

key_evidence.citation: Lim M et al. Current state of immunotherapy for glioblastoma. Nat Rev Clin Oncol. 2018.
Reardon DA et al. Immunotherapy advances for glioblastoma. Neuro Oncol. 2014.

protocol_claim_en: Any potential benefit of PD-1 or PD-L1 blockade in glioblastoma appears conditional on baseline tumor immune engagement and molecular context rather than universally applicable across patients.
risk_flags: Conditional framing; predictive biomarkers not prospectively validated; avoid patient-level predictions.

key_evidence.citation: Weathers SP et al. Nat Commun. 2025.
Lim M et al. Nat Rev Clin Oncol. 2018.

protocol_claim_en: Glioblastoma tumors are typically dominated by immunosuppressive myeloid cells (e.g., tumor-associated macrophages and microglia), which inhibit effective anti-tumor T-cell responses and limit the efficacy of immune checkpoint blockade.
risk_flags: Applies at population level; does not exclude rare T-cell–inflamed or treatment-modified tumors.

key_evidence.citation: Hambardzumyan D, Gutmann DH, Kettenmann H. The role of microglia and macrophages in glioma maintenance and progression. Nat Neurosci. 2016.
Lim M et al. Current state of immunotherapy for glioblastoma. Nat Rev Clin Oncol. 2018.

protocol_claim_en: In a subset of glioblastomas, higher baseline T-cell infiltration and immune activation signatures are associated with improved outcomes under immune checkpoint blockade, suggesting conditional susceptibility when effective anti-tumor T-cell activity is present.
risk_flags: Subset-specific; T-cell presence alone is insufficient; functional exhaustion and myeloid suppression may still dominate.

key_evidence.citation: Weathers SP et al. Improved overall survival in an anti-PD-L1 treated cohort of newly diagnosed glioblastoma patients. Nat Commun. 2025.
Cloughesy TF et al. Neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 immunotherapy promotes a survival benefit with intratumoral and systemic immune responses in recurrent glioblastoma. Nat Med. 2019.

protocol_claim_en: In diabetes populations, different glucose-lowering therapies may be associated with different cancer incidence risks, but causal interpretation is limited by confounding and bias in observational studies.
risk_flags: Mostly observational evidence; time-related biases and confounding by indication are common; not a basis for choosing therapy solely for cancer prevention.

key_evidence.citation: Cancer risk in diabetic patients treated with metformin: observational analysis.
Diabetes, cancer, and metformin: connections and possible mechanisms.

protocol_claim_en: Targeting mitochondrial metabolism and hypoxia-linked metabolic enzymes has been proposed as a therapeutic strategy; inhibition of key mitochondrial nodes can change redox state and tumor survival pathways in models.
risk_flags: Mechanistic/preclinical focus; clinical translation uncertain; hypoxia biology is complex and context-dependent.

key_evidence.citation: Inhibition of 2-oxoglutarate dehydrogenase as a metabolic vulnerability in hypoxia-linked contexts.

protocol_claim_en: Patient-derived in vivo functional testing platforms can be used to prioritize therapies and combinations by measuring tumor responses, supporting a precision oncology workflow.
risk_flags: Utility depends on validation, turnaround time, and how well models recapitulate human tumor microenvironment.

key_evidence.citation: In vivo functional platform targeting patient-derived tumors to guide therapy selection.

protocol_claim_en: Many solid tumors exhibit dependence on glutamine metabolism to support anaplerosis, redox balance, and nucleotide synthesis, creating potential metabolic vulnerabilities.
risk_flags: Context-dependent; tumors can rewire metabolism or use alternative carbon sources; glutamine dependence is not universal.

key_evidence.citation: DeBerardinis RJ, Cheng T. Q's next: the diverse functions of glutamine in metabolism, cell biology and cancer. Oncogene. 2010.

protocol_claim_en: Inhibition of glutaminase (GLS) can impair tumor growth in glutamine-dependent cancers, but compensatory metabolic pathways frequently limit sustained efficacy.
risk_flags: Metabolic plasticity and alternative anaplerotic pathways can bypass GLS inhibition; clinical benefit has been limited.

key_evidence.citation: Gross MI et al. Antitumor activity of the glutaminase inhibitor CB-839 in triple-negative breast cancer. Mol Cancer Ther. 2014.

protocol_claim_en: GLS2, a p53-regulated glutaminase isoform, can exert tumor-suppressive effects in some contexts, highlighting isoform-specific roles in glutamine metabolism.
risk_flags: Isoform effects are context-specific; GLS2 is not universally tumor suppressive; extrapolation across cancers is limited.

key_evidence.citation: Hu W et al. Glutaminase 2, a novel p53 target gene regulating energy metabolism and antioxidant function. PNAS. 2010.

protocol_claim_en: Hypoxic tumor microenvironments drive metabolic rewiring toward glycolysis and lactate production, contributing to immune suppression and resistance to immunotherapy.
risk_flags: Degree of hypoxia varies spatially; immune effects are multifactorial and not solely lactate-mediated.

key_evidence.citation: Fischer K et al. Inhibitory effect of tumor cell-derived lactic acid on human T cells. Blood. 2007.

protocol_claim_en: Lactate accumulation and acidification in the tumor microenvironment can impair cytotoxic T-cell and NK-cell function and may favor suppressive myeloid phenotypes.
risk_flags: Mechanistic dominance varies by tumor type; buffering alone does not reverse immune dysfunction.

key_evidence.citation: Brand A et al. LDHA-associated lactic acid production blunts tumor immunosurveillance by T and NK cells. Cell Metab. 2016.

protocol_claim_en: Myeloid-derived suppressor cells and tumor-associated macrophages use distinct metabolic programs that reinforce immune suppression within tumors.
risk_flags: Programs vary across myeloid subsets; targeting metabolism may affect normal immune cells.

key_evidence.citation: Ostrand-Rosenberg S, Fenselau C. Myeloid-derived suppressor cells: immune-suppressive cells that impair antitumor immunity. J Immunol. 2018.

protocol_claim_en: Metabolic interventions can modulate anti-tumor immunity, but isolated metabolic monotherapies rarely overcome established immunosuppressive networks in the tumor microenvironment.
risk_flags: Combination strategies are typically required; monotherapy effects are often transient.

key_evidence.citation: Buck MD et al. Metabolic instruction of immunity. Cell. 2017.

protocol_claim_en: Mitochondrial metabolic fitness supports sustained effector and memory T-cell function, and mitochondrial dysfunction contributes to T-cell exhaustion in tumors.
risk_flags: Primarily mechanistic evidence; translating mitochondrial modulation into therapy is complex.

key_evidence.citation: Scharping NE et al. Mitochondrial biogenesis promotes T cell memory formation. Cell. 2016.

protocol_claim_en: Tumor-driven metabolic competition for nutrients such as glucose and amino acids can deprive infiltrating T cells of resources required for effective anti-tumor activity.
risk_flags: Resource competition is one of several suppressive mechanisms; effects vary by nutrient and tumor context.

key_evidence.citation: Chang CH et al. Metabolic competition in the tumor microenvironment is a driver of cancer progression. Cell. 2015.

protocol_claim_en: Therapeutic targeting of cancer metabolism is most likely to succeed when combined with approaches that address immune suppression and resistance pathways, using rational scheduling and patient selection.
risk_flags: Combination toxicity and scheduling are major challenges; predictive biomarkers are limited.

key_evidence.citation: Pavlova NN, Thompson CB. The emerging hallmarks of cancer metabolism. Cell Metab. 2016.

protocol_claim_en: In malignant ureteral obstruction, one-year ureteral stent patency was higher with metallic stents than with polymeric stents (62.0% vs 48.5%).
risk_flags: Observational/retrospective; potential confounding by indication; single-center likely; patency endpoint not randomized.

key_evidence.citation: Nishi T et al. Comparison of clinical outcomes between metallic and polymeric ureteral stents in malignant ureteral obstruction: a retrospective comparative study. 2026. doi:10.1186/s12894-026-02062-z

protocol_claim_en: Operative time for ureteral stent insertion was longer with metallic stents than polymeric stents for both bilateral and unilateral placements.
risk_flags: Observational/retrospective; surgeon/complexity differences may confound operative time.

protocol_claim_en: Among patients with peritoneal dissemination and malignant ureteral obstruction, metallic stents had a longer patency period than polymeric stents.
risk_flags: Subgroup finding; observational; risk of selection bias and multiple comparisons.

protocol_claim_en: In the metallic-stent group, lower ureteral obstruction, direct tumor compression, pyuria, and elevated preoperative creatinine were associated with stent obstruction; in the polymeric-stent group, peritoneal dissemination was associated with obstruction.
risk_flags: Associations from retrospective analysis; multiple testing; unclear adjustment strategy.

protocol_claim_en: In diffuse large B-cell lymphoma models, P300 overexpression increased doxorubicin resistance while P300 silencing reduced doxorubicin resistance in vitro and in vivo.
risk_flags: Preclinical (cell lines/xenografts); translational uncertainty; mechanism-focused.

key_evidence.citation: Song X et al. P300 enhances glycolysis and dox resistance in DLBCL by upregulating HK2 expression through histone lactylation. 2026. doi:10.1186/s12885-026-15654-7

protocol_claim_en: P300-driven glycolysis increased lactate accumulation and histone lactylation at the HK2 promoter, promoting HK2 transcription via interaction with HIF-1.
risk_flags: Mechanistic preclinical evidence; pathway specificity may vary by context.

protocol_claim_en: Doxorubicin resistance in DLBCL was mediated by P300-facilitated glycolysis, per the study's functional and rescue experiments.
risk_flags: Preclinical; causal language should not be overgeneralized to patients.

protocol_claim_en: In a multi-center cross-sectional cohort, the prevalence of HPV-driven head and neck squamous cell carcinoma was approximately 11%.
risk_flags: Cross-sectional prevalence estimate; may not generalize beyond setting; depends on testing algorithm.

key_evidence.citation: Sathasivam HP et al. Human papillomavirus (HPV) - driven head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) in a multi-ethnic developing country. 2026. doi:10.1186/s12885-026-15550-0

protocol_claim_en: Most HPV-driven head and neck squamous cell carcinomas in the cohort arose in the oropharynx, with none reported from the oral cavity, larynx, or hypopharynx.
risk_flags: Cross-sectional; site distribution may reflect referral patterns; testing sensitivity differences by site.

protocol_claim_en: HPV16 was the most frequently observed genotype among HPV-driven head and neck squamous cell carcinomas in the cohort.
risk_flags: Cross-sectional genotype distribution; geographic variation expected.

protocol_claim_en: In a double-blind randomized trial of alpha-lipoic acid during head and neck radiotherapy, there were no significant between-group differences in salivary flow at follow-up points.
risk_flags: Small sample (n=20); limited power; short follow-up; outcome measurement variability.

key_evidence.citation: Anbari F et al. Effect of alpha-lipoic acid on salivary secretion in patients undergoing head and neck radiotherapy: a randomized clinical trial. 2026. doi:10.1186/s12885-026-15571-9

protocol_claim_en: Alpha-lipoic acid may temporarily delay early radiotherapy-associated salivary gland dysfunction, but the reported effect was not statistically significant and may not be sustained.
risk_flags: Interpretation statement; small RCT; effect not significant.

protocol_claim_en: Across multiple tumor types, CD26 (DPP4) expression was significantly upregulated in several cancers compared with normal tissues in an integrated pan-cancer analysis.
risk_flags: Bioinformatics/observational; depends on public datasets and normalization; correlation not causation.

key_evidence.citation: Tao R et al. The role of CD26 in breast cancer and its pan-cancer analysis. 2026. doi:10.1186/s12885-026-15656-5

protocol_claim_en: Higher CD26 expression was associated with advanced pathological stage and adverse prognosis in several tumor types (including breast cancer), while showing favorable associations in some tumors, suggesting context dependence.
risk_flags: Dataset-specific prognostic associations; confounding and multiple-testing risk; context-dependent effects.

protocol_claim_en: In vitro, pharmacologic CD26 inhibition with alogliptin reduced MCF-7 breast cancer cell proliferation and invasion and lowered MMP9 expression.
risk_flags: Cell-line evidence; dose/target specificity concerns; not direct clinical efficacy.

protocol_claim_en: In lung cancer patients, TP53 mutations were more frequently observed alongside microbial infections, whereas EGFR mutations were more common in patients without microbial infections.
risk_flags: Retrospective real-world data; infection ascertainment bias; confounding by clinical factors.

key_evidence.citation: Li T et al. A real-world evidence of sputum microbiota alterations and their association with oncogenomic changes and response to targeted therapies in patients with lung cancer. 2026. doi:10.1186/s12866-026-04773-7

protocol_claim_en: Tumors from infected patients showed higher tumor mutational burden and more frequent copy number variations (including on chromosome 11) compared with tumors from non-infected patients in the study.
risk_flags: Retrospective subset with NGS; causality unclear; multiple comparisons.

protocol_claim_en: Among patients with EGFR-mutant tumors, absence of concurrent microbial infection was associated with better objective response rates to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors and survival benefits.
risk_flags: Observational association; treatment selection and disease severity may confound.

protocol_claim_en: In paper-based electrochemiluminescent sensor substrates, office paper showed better electrochemical/sensor performance than highly porous filter paper, which caused signal loss.
risk_flags: Analytical methods paper; performance depends on assay conditions; not clinical outcomes.

key_evidence.citation: Kalligosfyri PM et al. Exploring the Feasibility of Paper-Based Substrates for User-Friendly Electrochemiluminescent Sensors. 2026. doi:10.1021/acs.analchem.5c06606

protocol_claim_en: Drying the coreactant tripropylamine onto paper substrates enabled elimination of manual reagent addition/mixing during analysis and improved procedural simplicity and storage stability in the described ECL system.
risk_flags: Bench/engineering claim; generalizability to other assays not guaranteed.

key_evidence.citation: Kalligosfyri PM et al. (2026) doi:10.1021/acs.analchem.5c06606

protocol_claim_en: Paper-based substrates, especially commercial office paper, were presented as sustainable and cost-effective platforms for ECL sensing with assessed sensitivity, stability, repeatability, and storage ability.
risk_flags: General conclusion statement; depends on local fabrication and measurement setup.

key_evidence.citation: Kalligosfyri PM et al. (2026) doi:10.1021/acs.analchem.5c06606

protocol_claim_en: TAM-like macrophages exhibited impaired release of small extracellular vesicles and reduced frequency of tetraspanin-positive particles compared with other macrophage subtypes.
risk_flags: In vitro polarization model; may not fully replicate patient TAM biology.

key_evidence.citation: Pörschke J et al. Tumor-associated macrophages display differential protein cargo sorting in extracellular vesicles associated with poor survival in ovarian cancer. 2026. doi:10.1186/s10020-025-01416-x

protocol_claim_en: Altered EV biogenesis/cargo in TAM-like macrophages was associated with changes in markers including decreased N-glycosylation of CD63, validated in patient-derived samples per the abstract.
risk_flags: Mechanistic biomarker claim; limited details in abstract; validation scope unclear.

protocol_claim_en: Proteins enriched in an ascites TAM-EV signature were mostly associated with poor prognosis, whereas M1-like EV-related markers were mostly associated with longer survival in ovarian cancer datasets.
risk_flags: Prognostic association from datasets; confounding; biomarker claims require external validation.

protocol_claim_en: After PD-1 inhibitor therapy in advanced NSCLC, sequential ramucirumab plus docetaxel achieved an objective response rate of 37.0%, median PFS of 5.1 months, and median OS of 10.4 months in a multicenter prospective cohort.
risk_flags: Small cohort (n=27 evaluable); non-randomized; landmark analysis considerations.

key_evidence.citation: Matsumoto K et al. Impact of Sequential Ramucirumab Plus Docetaxel After PD-1 Inhibitors on Anti-PD-1 Antibody-Bound T-Cell Dynamics and Clinical Outcomes. 2026. doi:10.1111/cas.70336

protocol_claim_en: Responders to ramucirumab plus docetaxel had higher IgG4+CD8+ T-cell and lower IgG4+ Treg T1/T0 ratios, and higher IgG4+CD8+ ratios were associated with longer landmark PFS and OS.
risk_flags: Biomarker dynamics; small sample; multiple testing; exploratory.

key_evidence.citation: Matsumoto K et al. (2026) doi:10.1111/cas.70336

protocol_claim_en: High baseline IgG4+CD8+ Temra and low VEGF-C levels at ramucirumab-plus-docetaxel initiation were independent prognostic factors for PFS and OS in multivariable analysis.
risk_flags: Exploratory prognostic biomarkers; small cohort; requires external validation.

key_evidence.citation: Matsumoto K et al. (2026) doi:10.1111/cas.70336

protocol_claim_en: The study suggests that administering ramucirumab plus docetaxel during persistent anti-PD-1 antibody binding on circulating T cells may be beneficial.
risk_flags: Mechanistic/interpretive conclusion; not proven causality; hypothesis-generating.

key_evidence.citation: Matsumoto K et al. (2026) doi:10.1111/cas.70336

protocol_claim_en: Post-tuberculosis bronchiectasis patients experienced more frequent acute exacerbations and had higher FACED and modified Reiff scores than non-post-TB bronchiectasis cases in a registry-based cohort.
risk_flags: Retrospective registry analysis; residual confounding; case definition differences.

key_evidence.citation: Ou WF et al. Lower FEV1 and gram-negative bacilli isolation as independent risk factors for exacerbations in post-TB bronchiectasis. 2026. doi:10.5588/ijtld.25.0336

protocol_claim_en: In post-TB bronchiectasis, FEV1 ≤ 60% predicted was an independent risk factor for acute exacerbations (aOR 2.334; 95% CI 1.192-4.572).
risk_flags: Observational; model specification and unmeasured confounding may affect estimates.

key_evidence.citation: Ou WF et al. (2026) doi:10.5588/ijtld.25.0336

protocol_claim_en: In post-TB bronchiectasis, gram-negative bacilli-positive sputum culture was an independent risk factor for acute exacerbations (aOR 3.075; 95% CI 1.362-6.942).
risk_flags: Observational; culture sampling bias; antibiotics and disease severity may confound.

key_evidence.citation: Ou WF et al. (2026) doi:10.5588/ijtld.25.0336

protocol_claim_en: In factorial vignette scenarios, alcohol consumption was rated as more acceptable than smoking in cancer contexts.
risk_flags: Survey/vignette design; cultural context dependent; acceptability is not a clinical outcome.

key_evidence.citation: Auriol C et al. Stigma in cancer: Comparing community and health professionals' acceptability of smoking and alcohol consumption. 2026. doi:10.1177/13591053261417030

protocol_claim_en: Healthcare professionals were slightly more accepting than the general public in judgments about smoking/drinking scenarios in cancer contexts.
risk_flags: Survey/vignette; selection bias; effect size not provided here.

protocol_claim_en: Stigma judgments about smoking decreased at advanced cancer stages in the study's scenarios.
risk_flags: Survey/vignette; interpretation depends on scenario framing.

protocol_claim_en: LukS-PV targeting C5aR inhibited epithelial-mesenchymal transition, migration, invasion, and lung metastasis in hepatocellular carcinoma models.
risk_flags: Preclinical; safety/feasibility in humans unknown; mechanism-focused.

key_evidence.citation: Ding P et al. LukS-PV targeting C5aR inhibits EMT in hepatocellular carcinoma via the BCL6/HDAC6/HSPD1 axis. 2026. doi:10.1038/s42003-026-09640-9

protocol_claim_en: Mechanistically, LukS-PV downregulated BCL6, reduced HDAC6 expression, increased HSPD1 acetylation, and promoted HSPD1 ubiquitin-mediated degradation, contributing to EMT inhibition.
risk_flags: Mechanistic chain inferred from preclinical assays; pathway complexity; replication needed.

protocol_claim_en: The study highlights the C5aR pathway as a potential therapeutic target in HCC EMT regulation based on LukS-PV activity.
risk_flags: Target/therapy implication; not clinical evidence; overgeneralization risk.

protocol_claim_en: In a network meta-analysis of 28 RCTs, acupoint stimulation therapies reduced cancer-related fatigue, with oil acupressure, relaxing acupressure, and acupuncture ranking highest by SUCRA.
risk_flags: Heterogeneity across trials; publication bias possible; network assumptions.

key_evidence.citation: Chou HC et al. Comparative Effectiveness of Acupoint Stimulation Therapies for Cancer-Related Fatigue: A Network Meta-Analysis. 2026. doi:10.1111/wvn.70104

protocol_claim_en: Self-administered acupressure was reported as similarly effective to professionally administered acupoint stimulation approaches for reducing cancer-related fatigue.
risk_flags: Based on subgroup comparisons; adherence and blinding limitations.

key_evidence.citation: Chou HC et al. (2026) doi:10.1111/wvn.70104

protocol_claim_en: The review suggests acupoint stimulation therapies can be integrated into routine cancer care as nonpharmacologic options for fatigue, with a need for standardized protocols and longer-term studies.
risk_flags: Practice implication; depends on availability/training; long-term outcomes uncertain.

key_evidence.citation: Chou HC et al. (2026) doi:10.1111/wvn.70104

protocol_claim_en: Single-cell profiling of mouse testes immune cells showed a decline of FOLR2+ resident macrophages and an increase in pro-inflammatory CD74+ macrophages, CCR2+ monocytes, and CD8+ T cells in aged mice.
risk_flags: Animal model; scRNA-seq interpretation; translation to humans uncertain.

key_evidence.citation: Li X et al. Single-cell immune atlas of mouse testes unveils metabolic reprogramming of FOLR2 + macrophages in orchestrating testicular immunity during aging. 2026. doi:10.1007/s11357-026-02109-x

protocol_claim_en: During testicular aging, FOLR2+ macrophages transitioned toward a pro-inflammatory state and were linked to recruitment of monocytes and CD8+ T cells via a CCL8-CCR2/CCR5 axis.
risk_flags: Mechanistic inference in mice; pathway generalization risk.

protocol_claim_en: Mitochondrial metabolic dysfunction was described as a driver of FOLR2+ macrophage activation during testicular aging, with IDH2 inhibition inducing activation.
risk_flags: Animal/cellular mechanism; causal direction may be context-dependent.

protocol_claim_en: A four-lncRNA oxidative stress-related signature (LINC02474, AL513550.1, SNHG16, AL161729.4) predicted prognosis in colorectal cancer and showed AUC 0.768 in the reported model.
risk_flags: Bioinformatics/modeling; risk of overfitting; external validation needed.

key_evidence.citation: Chen P et al. A new oxidative stress-related lncRNA signature predicts the prognosis of colorectal cancer patients. 2026. doi:10.1007/s12672-026-04496-1

protocol_claim_en: The oxidative stress-related lncRNA risk score was presented as outperforming conventional clinicopathological parameters for prognostic prediction in the study.
risk_flags: Comparative performance may depend on modeling choices; needs external cohorts.

protocol_claim_en: High-risk colorectal cancer patients were predicted to be more sensitive to several drugs (e.g., ABT.263, AZD.0530, gefitinib, imatinib, PAC.1, shikonin) in the reported analysis.
risk_flags: In silico drug sensitivity inference; not clinical response evidence.

protocol_claim_en: A competing-risk nomogram for cancer-specific death in children/adolescents with lymphoma showed AUCs around 0.855 (1-year) in training and 0.862 (1-year) in testing cohorts in the study.
risk_flags: SEER-based modeling; retrospective; needs external validation; outcome coding limitations.

key_evidence.citation: Ding T et al. Construction and validation of nomogram for the cancer-specific death in children and adolescents-onset lymphoma. 2026. doi:10.1007/s12672-026-04556-6

protocol_claim_en: Age, race, year of diagnosis, pathological subtype, tumor grade, tumor stage, and chemotherapy were identified as independent factors associated with cancer-specific death risk in the lymphoma cohort.
risk_flags: Registry observational modeling; confounding and missing variables; treatment indication bias.

protocol_claim_en: Calibration and decision curve analyses suggested the nomogram had good agreement and clinical utility in the reported training and validation cohorts.
risk_flags: Model utility claims depend on assumptions; external validation required.

protocol_claim_en: This review argues BioBran/MGN-3 (a standardized arabinoxylan concentrate) has immunomodulatory activity and is proposed as a complementary therapy alongside conventional cancer treatments.
risk_flags: Complementary-therapy framing; product/supplement claims; evidence base includes heterogeneous study types; avoid implying proven benefit for all cancers.

key_evidence.citation: Ooi SL et al. Evidence-Based Review of BioBran/MGN-3 Arabinoxylan Compound as a Complementary Therapy for Conventional Cancer Treatment. Integr Cancer Ther. 2017. PMID: 29037071. doi:10.1177/1534735417735379

protocol_claim_en: In vitro studies summarized in the review report immunomodulating and/or synergistic anti-cancer effects of MGN-3 when combined with chemotherapeutic agents.
risk_flags: In vitro only; synergy in cell lines does not imply clinical benefit; do not extrapolate dosing or outcomes to humans.

key_evidence.citation: Ooi SL et al. Integr Cancer Ther. 2017: review results describe in vitro synergistic effects with chemotherapeutic agents. PMID: 29037071.

protocol_claim_en: Animal (murine) models summarized in the review report MGN-3 may inhibit tumor growth and/or act against carcinogenic agents, either alone or with other anticancer compounds.
risk_flags: Animal-model evidence; results may not translate to humans; do not claim efficacy in patients.

key_evidence.citation: Ooi SL et al. Integr Cancer Ther. 2017: review results describe murine model findings including inhibition of tumor growth. PMID: 29037071.

risk_flags: Retrospective single-center cohort; limited events; residual confounding possible; grading subject to interobserver variability.

key_evidence.citation: Zeyveli Çelik N et al. Prognostic determinants of survival in early-stage endometrial cancer: A retrospective analysis. Turk J Obstet Gynecol. 2026. PMID:41608872.

protocol_claim_en: In the same early-stage endometrial cancer cohort, elevated preoperative CA-125 levels were associated with worse overall survival on univariate analysis but were not independent predictors after multivariate adjustment.

key_evidence.citation: Zeyveli Çelik N et al. Turk J Obstet Gynecol. 2026. PMID:41608872.

protocol_claim_en: Adjuvant radiotherapy or chemotherapy did not show a statistically significant improvement in overall or disease-free survival in this retrospective early-stage endometrial cancer cohort.
risk_flags: Non-randomized treatment allocation; selection bias; treatment heterogeneity; limited power for subgroup effects.

key_evidence.citation: Zeyveli Çelik N et al. Turk J Obstet Gynecol. 2026. PMID:41608872.

protocol_claim_en: In early-stage endometrial cancer, histologic grade appeared to be a stronger prognostic factor than depth of myometrial invasion or lymphovascular space invasion in the reported analysis.
risk_flags: Comparative strength based on one cohort; pathologic assessment variability; not a substitute for formal staging guidelines.

key_evidence.citation: Zeyveli Çelik N et al. Turk J Obstet Gynecol. 2026. PMID:41608872.

protocol_claim_en: Myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) accumulate in many cancers and actively suppress anti-tumor T-cell responses, contributing to immune evasion and tumor progression.
risk_flags: Broad category; MDSC phenotypes and impact vary by tumor type and stage.

key_evidence.citation: Myeloid-Derived Suppressor Cells in Cancer: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Implications. Immune Network.

protocol_claim_en: MDSCs are a heterogeneous population of immature myeloid cells that expand during cancer and other pathological conditions, and they suppress T-cell activation through various mechanisms including arginase-1 production, reactive oxygen species generation, and immunosuppressive cytokine secretion.
risk_flags: Mechanistic details may vary by MDSC subset and tumor context.

key_evidence.citation: Myeloid-Derived Suppressor Cells in Cancer: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Implications. Immune Network.

protocol_claim_en: Expansion and activation of MDSCs are driven by tumor-derived inflammatory signals and growth factors, linking chronic inflammation to immune suppression in cancer.
risk_flags: Inflammatory drivers are context-dependent; causality in humans is complex.

key_evidence.citation: Tumor-induced expansion of myeloid-derived suppressor cells. Immune Network.

protocol_claim_en: Therapeutic strategies targeting MDSCs in cancer include inhibiting their recruitment to tumors, blocking their immunosuppressive functions, promoting their differentiation into non-suppressive cells, and depleting them using chemotherapeutic agents or antibodies.
risk_flags: Many strategies are in preclinical stages; clinical efficacy and safety remain to be established.

key_evidence.citation: Myeloid-Derived Suppressor Cells in Cancer: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Implications. Immune Network.

protocol_claim_en: T cell exhaustion in tumors is tightly linked to metabolic insufficiency, including reduced glycolysis and impaired mitochondrial function.
risk_flags: Predominantly mechanistic evidence; exhaustion phenotypes vary across tumor types and therapies.

key_evidence.citation: Metabolic regulation of T cell exhaustion and anti-tumor immunity. Front Immunol. 2020.

protocol_claim_en: Competition for nutrients such as glucose and amino acids within the tumor microenvironment limits T cell effector function and promotes exhaustion.
risk_flags: Nutrient competition is one of several suppressive mechanisms; relative importance is context-dependent.

key_evidence.citation: Frontiers in Immunology review on metabolic competition and T cell dysfunction. 2020.

protocol_claim_en: Mitochondrial dysfunction and defective biogenesis contribute to loss of T cell persistence and memory formation in tumors.
risk_flags: Translation into therapeutic modulation remains complex; mitochondrial effects may differ across T cell subsets.

key_evidence.citation: Metabolic control of exhausted T cells in cancer. Front Immunol. 2020.

protocol_claim_en: Reprogramming T cell metabolism may enhance responses to immune checkpoint blockade, but metabolic interventions alone are rarely sufficient.
risk_flags: Combination strategies required; optimal timing and patient selection remain unresolved.

key_evidence.citation: Frontiers in Immunology review on metabolic modulation and immunotherapy. 2020.

protocol_claim_en: Tumor-intrinsic metabolic reprogramming reshapes the tumor microenvironment in ways that suppress anti-tumor immune responses.
risk_flags: General framework claim; specific suppressive mechanisms vary across tumor types.

key_evidence.citation: Tumor Metabolism and Immune Suppression. Front Immunol. 2020.

protocol_claim_en: Depletion of nutrients such as glucose, amino acids, and lipids by tumor cells can directly impair effector T-cell and NK-cell function.
risk_flags: Relative importance of specific nutrients differs by immune subset and tumor context.

key_evidence.citation: Frontiers in Immunology review on nutrient depletion and immune dysfunction. 2020.

protocol_claim_en: Accumulation of tumor-derived metabolites such as lactate and adenosine promotes immunosuppressive phenotypes and inhibits cytotoxic immune responses.
risk_flags: Metabolite dominance varies spatially within tumors; not all immune suppression is metabolite-driven.

key_evidence.citation: Tumor-derived metabolites and immune suppression. Front Immunol. 2020.

protocol_claim_en: Effective cancer immunotherapy will likely require simultaneous targeting of tumor metabolism and immune checkpoints to overcome metabolic immune suppression.
risk_flags: Combination toxicity and scheduling challenges; predictive biomarkers remain limited.

key_evidence.citation: Metabolic modulation as an adjunct to immunotherapy. Front Immunol. 2020.
